front_blocks.md: Define **marketing**.

back_blocks.md: The aim of **marketing** is to **identify, anticipate and satisfy consumer needs and wants profitably**.

cards.front_md: Define **marketing**.
cards.back_md: The aim of **marketing** is to **identify, anticipate and satisfy consumer needs and wants profitably**.

front_blocks.md: What is the difference between a customer 'need' and a 'want'?

back_blocks.md: A **need** is essential (e.g. food, shelter); a **want** is a **non-essential** desire (e.g. Nike trainers).

cards.front_md: What is the difference between a customer 'need' and a 'want'?
cards.back_md: A **need** is essential (e.g. food, shelter); a **want** is a **non-essential** desire (e.g. Nike trainers).

front_blocks.md: Give two things marketing helps a business find out about its customers.

back_blocks.md: The **variety/quality** they want, the **price** they'll pay, effective **promotion**, and **where/how** they want to buy (any two).

cards.front_md: Give two things marketing helps a business find out about its customers.
cards.back_md: The **variety/quality** they want, the **price** they'll pay, effective **promotion**, and **where/how** they want to buy (any two).

front_blocks.md: Define **customer loyalty**.

back_blocks.md: **Customer loyalty** is when **existing customers buy from the same business over and over again**.

cards.front_md: Define **customer loyalty**.
cards.back_md: **Customer loyalty** is when **existing customers buy from the same business over and over again**.

front_blocks.md: Why is keeping existing customers cheaper than gaining new ones?

back_blocks.md: Gaining new customers needs **expensive advertising**, whereas loyal customers can be kept more cheaply (e.g. with **loyalty cards**).

cards.front_md: Why is keeping existing customers cheaper than gaining new ones?
cards.back_md: Gaining new customers needs **expensive advertising**, whereas loyal customers can be kept more cheaply (e.g. with **loyalty cards**).

front_blocks.md: Define **market orientation**.

back_blocks.md: **Market orientation** focuses on the **needs of consumers**, using that information to **design products that meet those needs**.

cards.front_md: Define **market orientation**.
cards.back_md: **Market orientation** focuses on the **needs of consumers**, using that information to **design products that meet those needs**.

front_blocks.md: Define **product orientation**.

back_blocks.md: **Product orientation** focuses on the **product itself** rather than consumer needs — creating a product first, then finding a market.

cards.front_md: Define **product orientation**.
cards.back_md: **Product orientation** focuses on the **product itself** rather than consumer needs — creating a product first, then finding a market.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
A business that is too product-orientated risks moving away from what the market wants.

back_blocks.md: **True.**
Over time it can move **further from what the market is looking for**, increasing the risk of **failure**.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

A business that is too product-orientated risks moving away from what the market wants.
cards.back_md:
**True.**

Over time it can move **further from what the market is looking for**, increasing the risk of **failure**.

front_blocks.md: Define a **niche market**.

back_blocks.md: A **niche market** is a **small subset** of a larger market whose specific demands a business satisfies (e.g. gluten-free bread).

cards.front_md: Define a **niche market**.
cards.back_md: A **niche market** is a **small subset** of a larger market whose specific demands a business satisfies (e.g. gluten-free bread).

front_blocks.md: Define a **mass market**.

back_blocks.md: A **mass market** aims products at **broad market segments** and most of the available market (e.g. Kellogg's Corn Flakes).

cards.front_md: Define a **mass market**.
cards.back_md: A **mass market** aims products at **broad market segments** and most of the available market (e.g. Kellogg's Corn Flakes).

front_blocks.md: Why can niche market products often charge high prices?

back_blocks.md: **Small-scale** production means **high average costs** (no economies of scale), but **specialised, unique** products let firms charge **high prices** and earn higher margins.

cards.front_md: Why can niche market products often charge high prices?
cards.back_md: **Small-scale** production means **high average costs** (no economies of scale), but **specialised, unique** products let firms charge **high prices** and earn higher margins.

front_blocks.md: Mass market products have low average costs because large-scale production benefits from economies of <u>  </u>.

back_blocks.md: Mass market products have low average costs because large-scale production benefits from economies of **scale**.

front_blocks.md: What is the formula for market share?

back_blocks.md: **Market share = (sales of the business ÷ market size) × 100**.

cards.front_md: What is the formula for market share?
cards.back_md: **Market share = (sales of the business ÷ market size) × 100**.

front_blocks.md: What is the formula for market growth?

back_blocks.md: **Market growth = ((this year's sales − last year's sales) ÷ last year's sales) × 100**.

cards.front_md: What is the formula for market growth?
cards.back_md: **Market growth = ((this year's sales − last year's sales) ÷ last year's sales) × 100**.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
A negative market growth rate means the market is expanding.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
A **negative** rate means the market is **contracting** (getting smaller); a **positive** rate means it is **expanding**.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

A negative market growth rate means the market is expanding.
cards.back_md:
**False.**

A **negative** rate means the market is **contracting** (getting smaller); a **positive** rate means it is **expanding**.

front_blocks.md: Market share measures the <u>  </u> of total market revenue that one business or brand holds.

back_blocks.md: Market share measures the **percentage** of total market revenue that one business or brand holds.

front_blocks.md: Name three reasons customer spending patterns change.

back_blocks.md: Changes in **tastes and fashions**, **disposable incomes**, **demographics**, **global influences**, and **technology** (any three).

cards.front_md: Name three reasons customer spending patterns change.
cards.back_md: Changes in **tastes and fashions**, **disposable incomes**, **demographics**, **global influences**, and **technology** (any three).

front_blocks.md: How can a fall in disposable income affect spending?

back_blocks.md: High **unemployment or inflation** may lead customers to buy **cheaper products** (e.g. own-brand cereal).

cards.front_md: How can a fall in disposable income affect spending?
cards.back_md: High **unemployment or inflation** may lead customers to buy **cheaper products** (e.g. own-brand cereal).

front_blocks.md: Give an example of technology changing spending patterns.

back_blocks.md: New technology makes old technology obsolete — e.g. **smart speakers replacing radios**.

cards.front_md: Give an example of technology changing spending patterns.
cards.back_md: New technology makes old technology obsolete — e.g. **smart speakers replacing radios**.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
If a business fails to respond to changing customer needs, it is likely to fail.

back_blocks.md: **True.**
Markets change constantly, so a business that does **not respond** to changing needs is **likely to fail**.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

If a business fails to respond to changing customer needs, it is likely to fail.
cards.back_md:
**True.**

Markets change constantly, so a business that does **not respond** to changing needs is **likely to fail**.

front_blocks.md: Define **competition** (in a market).

back_blocks.md: **Competition** occurs when **at least two businesses** provide goods or services to the **same target market**.

cards.front_md: Define **competition** (in a market).
cards.back_md: **Competition** occurs when **at least two businesses** provide goods or services to the **same target market**.

front_blocks.md: Give two benefits of competition for customers.

back_blocks.md: **Lower prices**, **better-quality products**, and **better customer service**.

cards.front_md: Give two benefits of competition for customers.
cards.back_md: **Lower prices**, **better-quality products**, and **better customer service**.

front_blocks.md: Why have many markets become more competitive in recent years?

back_blocks.md: **Globalisation**, cheaper **transport**, the **internet and e-commerce**, and more **consumer information**.

cards.front_md: Why have many markets become more competitive in recent years?
cards.back_md: **Globalisation**, cheaper **transport**, the **internet and e-commerce**, and more **consumer information**.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
A lack of competition gives businesses a strong incentive to innovate and cut prices.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
The **absence of competition reduces** incentives to innovate, be efficient or lower prices.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

A lack of competition gives businesses a strong incentive to innovate and cut prices.
cards.back_md:
**False.**

The **absence of competition reduces** incentives to innovate, be efficient or lower prices.

front_blocks.md: Name two steps a business can take to stay competitive.

back_blocks.md: **New product development**, strong **customer focus**, **improving products**, and **minimising costs** (any two).

cards.front_md: Name two steps a business can take to stay competitive.
cards.back_md: **New product development**, strong **customer focus**, **improving products**, and **minimising costs** (any two).

front_blocks.md: How can minimising costs help a business stay competitive?

back_blocks.md: **Lower costs can be passed on** as lower prices, and extra retained profit can fund **promotion or expansion**.

cards.front_md: How can minimising costs help a business stay competitive?
cards.back_md: **Lower costs can be passed on** as lower prices, and extra retained profit can fund **promotion or expansion**.

front_blocks.md: Developing new and innovative products encourages customer <u>  </u> and attracts new customers.

back_blocks.md: Developing new and innovative products encourages customer **loyalty** and attracts new customers.

cards.front_md: Developing new and innovative products encourages customer <u>  </u> and attracts new customers.
cards.back_md: Developing new and innovative products encourages customer **loyalty** and attracts new customers.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
Competition only exists when there are many businesses in a market.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
Competition exists with **at least two** businesses; the **more** there are, the **more intense** it becomes.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

Competition only exists when there are many businesses in a market.

**False.**

front_blocks.md: Give an example of a global influence changing a market.

back_blocks.md: The arrival of international brands — e.g. **American fast-food chains** now dominating fast food across Europe.

cards.front_md: Give an example of a global influence changing a market.

front_blocks.md: Define **market segmentation**.

back_blocks.md: **Market segmentation** is dividing a **single market into groups**, each with **distinct customer preferences**.

cards.front_md: Define **market segmentation**.
cards.back_md: **Market segmentation** is dividing a **single market into groups**, each with **distinct customer preferences**.

front_blocks.md: Why do businesses use market segmentation?

back_blocks.md: To **target marketing** at the customers most likely to buy — an **efficient use of budget** that closely meets **customer needs**.

cards.front_md: Why do businesses use market segmentation?
cards.back_md: To **target marketing** at the customers most likely to buy — an **efficient use of budget** that closely meets **customer needs**.

front_blocks.md: How can segmentation increase customer loyalty?

back_blocks.md: When customers feel their **needs are met**, they are more likely to be **loyal** and to **recommend the brand**.

cards.front_md: How can segmentation increase customer loyalty?
cards.back_md: When customers feel their **needs are met**, they are more likely to be **loyal** and to **recommend the brand**.

front_blocks.md: Name three ways a market can be segmented.

back_blocks.md: **Location**, **demographics**, **lifestyle**, **income**, and **age** (any three).

cards.front_md: Name three ways a market can be segmented.
cards.back_md: **Location**, **demographics**, **lifestyle**, **income**, and **age** (any three).

front_blocks.md: Give an example of segmenting a market by location.

back_blocks.md: **City-dwellers** may buy **small electric cars**, while **rural** customers prefer **larger, all-terrain vehicles**.

cards.front_md: Give an example of segmenting a market by location.
cards.back_md: **City-dwellers** may buy **small electric cars**, while **rural** customers prefer **larger, all-terrain vehicles**.

front_blocks.md: How might a market be segmented by demographics?

back_blocks.md: By **gender**, the **age of the population**, or **ethnicity/religion** — e.g. clothing and food targeted at specific groups.

cards.front_md: How might a market be segmented by demographics?
cards.back_md: By **gender**, the **age of the population**, or **ethnicity/religion** — e.g. clothing and food targeted at specific groups.

front_blocks.md: Give one advantage of market segmentation.

back_blocks.md: Marketing can be **targeted precisely** at different groups, which is **less wasteful** and can **increase loyalty**.

cards.front_md: Give one advantage of market segmentation.
cards.back_md: Marketing can be **targeted precisely** at different groups, which is **less wasteful** and can **increase loyalty**.

front_blocks.md: Give one disadvantage of market segmentation.

back_blocks.md: A segment may be **hard to identify** or **too small to be profitable**, and it needs **costly, detailed market research**.

cards.front_md: Give one disadvantage of market segmentation.
cards.back_md: A segment may be **hard to identify** or **too small to be profitable**, and it needs **costly, detailed market research**.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
Every consumer belongs to only one market segment.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
Consumers can belong to **multiple segments** at the same time, which makes segments hard to identify.

**True or False?**

**False.**

front_blocks.md: Name two factors a business considers when choosing a method of segmentation.

back_blocks.md: **Brand image**, the **cost of entry** into the segment, and **market analysis data**.

cards.front_md: Name two factors a business considers when choosing a method of segmentation.

front_blocks.md: Why must a chosen segment align with a business's brand image?

back_blocks.md: Appealing to the wrong segment can **harm the image** — e.g. a **luxury retailer** targeting a **budget market**.

cards.front_md: Why must a chosen segment align with a business's brand image?

back_blocks.md: **False.**
